This is a little misleading. The main difference between compE and compSci degrees is the amount of courses or projects you take that are more EE oriented. In my compsci degree, I still took signals, comp architecture, and gpu architecture courses. Those are hardware focused. Sure I don’t build circuits or design wafers for a job, but I still know how a computer works to a good degree. In fact I designed one in simulation with a decent OS on top 😅 A computer scientist that doesn’t know what an ALU is or how memory works or what the point of a TLB is or how superscalar ISAs work or how branch prediction works in hardware is taking a fake computer sci degree IMO.
